body: Wheeler, Munger & Co. partnership 1962-1975: ~19.8% a year vs ~5% for the Dow (Buffett's 1984 'Superinvestors' article), but with -31.9% in 1973 and -31.5% in 1974 (figures from that article; not re-checked here) - proof that concentration brings deep drawdowns. Berkshire vice-chairman from 1978; he pushed Buffett from Graham cigar butts to 'wonderful companies at fair prices' (See's Candies 1972). Signature trades: BYD - Berkshire's 2008 stake (~225m shares, ~$230-270m depending on source) became worth ~$8-9bn by 2023 per Munger, ~39x over 17 years per later reports, mostly sold 2022-25; Daily Journal sold part of its BYD holding in late 2021 at ~15x cost. Process edge: a 'latticework' of models from psychology, economics, biology and engineering; inversion ('tell me where I'll die so I never go there'); his 1995 'Psychology of Human Misjudgment' list of biases; extreme patience ('sit on your ass investing') and very few bets. Mistakes: Alibaba bought at Daily Journal in 2021 - he later called it one of his worst mistakes; early partnership drawdowns. Died Nov 2023 aged 99. Copyable: a pre-mortem/inversion checklist before every buy, a written bias list, and the willingness to hold cash until a rare fat pitch appears.
title: Charlie Munger - mental models, inversion, and patience for few great bets

body: Flag: SEVERE. Cement-hydro-real-estate-expressway group that borrowed heavily in 2007-2012. Jaypee Infratech (JIL, Yamuna Expressway + ~20,000+ unfinished Noida flats) was among RBI's first 12 IBC referrals (2017, IDBI-led); its listed equity was extinguished; NCLT approved Suraksha group's plan (Mar-2023). Key finding: the Supreme Court (Feb-2020, Anuj Jain v Axis Bank) upheld that JIL's mortgage of ~858 acres to secure the parent Jaiprakash Associates' (JAL) loans were preferential transactions to be avoided -- a listed subsidiary's assets pledged for the parent's debt. Homebuyer funds: ED arrested MD Manoj Gaur (13-Nov-2025) alleging ~Rs 12,000 cr of homebuyer money was diverted/siphoned, partly to Jaypee Sewa Sansthan (a trust he heads); he reportedly surrendered in Feb-2026 after bail rejection (single-source). Charges are allegations pending trial. JAL itself went into IBC; CoC approved Adani Enterprises' ~Rs 14,535 cr plan with 93.8% votes (Nov-2025), NCLT approved (17-Mar-2026), NCLAT dismissed Vedanta's challenge (4-May-2026) -- JAL equity holders expected to get little or nothing. Jaiprakash Power Ventures went through lender-led debt-for-equity conversion and remains listed. Early signals (visible by 2012-14): customer advances funding other businesses, inter-group guarantees and mortgages, repeated asset sales to service debt, rising promoter pledges. Lesson: in real-estate groups, homebuyer advances are the first pot of money diverted.

data.allegations: ED 2025: Rs 12,000 cr homebuyer-fund diversion (pending trial)
data.regulator_findings: SC 2020: JIL mortgages for JAL = preferential transactions
data.status_2026: JAL to Adani via IBC (NCLAT May-2026); JIL with Suraksha

title: Jaypee group (Jaiprakash Gaur / Manoj Gaur) — governance history

body: Flag: SEVERE (unlisted; included as a governance pattern for future IPO candidates). Think & Learn peaked at a ~$22bn private valuation (2022) after debt-funded acquisitions (Aakash ~$950m, WhiteHat Jr, Great Learning, Epic). Signals: FY21 accounts filed ~18 months late; auditor Deloitte resigned (Jun-2023) citing delays, and three board members (Peak XV, Prosus, Chan Zuckerberg nominees) quit the same week; $1.2bn term-loan B default and lender litigation in the US; ~$533m from Byju's Alpha (the TLB borrower) moved to a small US hedge fund (Camshaft Capital) and onward offshore, per lenders; ED alleged FEMA violations of ~Rs 9,000 cr (Nov-2023 notice). BCCI's petition put Think & Learn into Indian insolvency (2024); a settlement with BCCI was set aside by the Supreme Court route (the SC dismissed Raveendran's plea on the BCCI settlement). A Delaware bankruptcy court entered a >$1bn default judgment against Raveendran personally (Nov-2025) for failing discovery; it was later corrected to say damages had not been determined, with a damages phase set for Jan-2026 (outcome not found). Aakash, now separately controlled by Manipal's Ranjan Pai, blocked transactions with Think & Learn. Raveendran denies wrongdoing. Lesson: late audited accounts, auditor exit plus investor-director exits in the same week are near-certain distress signals; debt at an offshore SPV with founder control of cash is a severe risk.

data.regulator_findings: US court default judgment (Nov-2025, later corrected); ED FEMA notice (allegation)
data.status_2026: Think & Learn in insolvency; US damages phase pending
